```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)
library(readr)

# IPEDS categories, in IPEDS order. Making race and gender factors with
# these levels means every table shows every row, including zeros.
race_levels <- c("Nonresident", "Hispanic/Latino", "American Indian or Alaska Native",
                 "Asian", "Black or African American", "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander",
                 "White", "Two or more races", "Race/ethnicity unknown")
gender_levels <- c("Men", "Women")

# One table shape for every Part A line: race down, gender across, totals.
by_race_gender <- function(df) {
  df |>
    count(race, gender, .drop = FALSE) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = gender, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    mutate(Total = Men + Women)
}

# The upload data frame. Every question appends its rows here.
upload <- tibble(part = character(), line = character(), cell = character(), value = numeric())
add_rows <- function(part, line, df) {
  # df has columns cell and value
  upload <<- bind_rows(upload, tibble(part = part, line = line, cell = df$cell, value = df$value))
  invisible(df)
}
```

::: {.callout-important title="This is a template on fake data"}
The population chunk below invents 3,000 students so the document renders
anywhere. To use it, replace that one chunk with the population query
against your warehouse (an example is in the chunk after it, not run).
Every question section stays exactly as it is.
:::

# The population

One query builds every student who could count for this survey, with every
column any question needs. The questions never touch the database; they
filter this.

**Rule.** Students enrolled for credit as of the fall census date
(`r params$census_term`). One row per student. Columns are IPEDS
categories, not Banner codes: the mapping from codes to categories happens
here, once, and nowhere else.

```{r}
#| label: population-fake
set.seed(params$report_year)
n <- 3000
pop <- tibble(
  id          = sprintf("S%05d", seq_len(n)),
  level       = sample(c("Undergraduate", "Graduate"), n, TRUE, c(0.8, 0.2)),
  attendance  = sample(c("Full-time", "Part-time"), n, TRUE, c(0.85, 0.15)),
  gender      = sample(c("Men", "Women"), n, TRUE),
  race        = sample(c("Nonresident", "Hispanic/Latino", "American Indian or Alaska Native",
                         "Asian", "Black or African American", "Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander",
                         "White", "Two or more races", "Race/ethnicity unknown"),
                       n, TRUE, c(0.06, 0.05, 0.005, 0.03, 0.07, 0.002, 0.68, 0.04, 0.063)),
  first_time  = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n, TRUE, c(0.25, 0.75)),
  degree_seeking = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), n, TRUE, c(0.97, 0.03)),
  age         = pmax(17, round(rnorm(n, 22, 4)))
) |>
  mutate(first_time = first_time & level == "Undergraduate",
         race   = factor(race, levels = race_levels),
         gender = factor(gender, levels = gender_levels))
```

```{r}
#| label: population-real
#| eval: false
# The real thing. Column names in the SELECT are the IPEDS categories the
# questions use, so nothing below has to know what the codes were.
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "MY_DSN",
                      UID = "my_user", PWD = keyring::key_get("my_service", "my_user"))
pop <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT student_id                                   AS id,
         CASE WHEN level_code = 'UG' THEN 'Undergraduate' ELSE 'Graduate' END AS level,
         CASE WHEN credit_hours >= 12 OR (level_code <> 'UG' AND credit_hours >= 9)
              THEN 'Full-time' ELSE 'Part-time' END   AS attendance,
         ipeds_gender                                 AS gender,
         ipeds_race_category                          AS race,
         CASE WHEN first_time_flag = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS first_time,
         CASE WHEN degree_seeking_flag = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS degree_seeking,
         age_on_census_date                           AS age
    FROM my_schema.fall_census_enrollment
   WHERE term_code = ?", params = list(params$census_term)) |>
  mutate(first_time = first_time == 1, degree_seeking = degree_seeking == 1,
         race   = factor(race, levels = race_levels),
         gender = factor(gender, levels = gender_levels))
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

```{r}
#| label: population-summary
tibble(What = c("Students in the population", "Undergraduate", "Graduate", "First-time undergraduates"),
       Count = c(nrow(pop), sum(pop$level == "Undergraduate"), sum(pop$level == "Graduate"), sum(pop$first_time))) |>
  gt() |> fmt_number(Count, decimals = 0) |> tab_options(column_labels.hidden = TRUE)
```

# Part A, line 1: full-time first-time degree-seeking undergraduates

::: {.callout-note title="IPEDS asks"}
**Part A, Line 1.** Full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking
undergraduate students, by race/ethnicity and gender.
:::

**Rule.** Undergraduate level; attending full-time (12 or more credit
hours); first-time as IPEDS defines it (no prior postsecondary enrollment
after high school, with the summer-start exception applied in the
population query); degree-seeking. Counted once each, in the race category
from the population.

```{r}
#| label: ef-a-1
a1 <- pop |>
  filter(level == "Undergraduate", attendance == "Full-time", first_time, degree_seeking) |>
  by_race_gender()

a1 |> gt(rowname_col = "race") |> grand_summary_rows(columns = c(Men, Women, Total), fns = list(Total = ~ sum(.)), fmt = ~ fmt_number(., decimals = 0))

add_rows("A", "1", a1 |> pivot_longer(c(Men, Women), names_to = "gender", values_to = "value") |>
           mutate(cell = paste(race, gender, sep = " | ")) |> select(cell, value))
```

# Part A, line 7: all full-time undergraduates

::: {.callout-note title="IPEDS asks"}
**Part A, Line 7.** Total full-time undergraduate students, by
race/ethnicity and gender.
:::

**Rule.** Undergraduate level; full-time. First-time or not, degree-seeking
or not. Line 1 is a subset of this line, which the checks section verifies.

```{r}
#| label: ef-a-7
a7 <- pop |>
  filter(level == "Undergraduate", attendance == "Full-time") |>
  by_race_gender()

a7 |> gt(rowname_col = "race") |> grand_summary_rows(columns = c(Men, Women, Total), fns = list(Total = ~ sum(.)), fmt = ~ fmt_number(., decimals = 0))

add_rows("A", "7", a7 |> pivot_longer(c(Men, Women), names_to = "gender", values_to = "value") |>
           mutate(cell = paste(race, gender, sep = " | ")) |> select(cell, value))
```

# Part B: enrollment by age

::: {.callout-note title="IPEDS asks"}
**Part B.** Enrollment by age category, attendance status, and level.
(Required in odd-numbered years.)
:::

**Rule.** Age on the census date, in the IPEDS bands. A student whose age
is unknown goes in "Age unknown", which the population query would supply
as NA.

```{r}
#| label: ef-b
b <- pop |>
  mutate(age_band = case_when(
    is.na(age) ~ "Age unknown",
    age < 18   ~ "Under 18",
    age <= 19  ~ "18-19",
    age <= 21  ~ "20-21",
    age <= 24  ~ "22-24",
    age <= 29  ~ "25-29",
    age <= 34  ~ "30-34",
    age <= 39  ~ "35-39",
    age <= 49  ~ "40-49",
    age <= 64  ~ "50-64",
    TRUE       ~ "65 and over")) |>
  count(level, attendance, age_band) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(level, attendance), values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

b |> gt(rowname_col = "age_band") |> tab_spanner_delim(delim = "_")

add_rows("B", "all", b |> pivot_longer(-age_band, names_to = "col", values_to = "value") |>
           mutate(cell = paste(age_band, col, sep = " | ")) |> select(cell, value))
```

# Checks

A submission that does not reconcile should not render. These stop the
document if they fail.

```{r}
#| label: checks
#| echo: true
# Line 1 is a subset of line 7, race by race (joined by name, never by position).
cmp <- inner_join(a1, a7, by = "race", suffix = c("_l1", "_l7"))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == length(race_levels), all(cmp$Total_l1 <= cmp$Total_l7))

# Part A line 7 total equals the full-time undergraduate count in the population.
stopifnot(sum(a7$Total) == sum(pop$level == "Undergraduate" & pop$attendance == "Full-time"))

# Part B totals equal the population.
stopifnot(sum(b[-1]) == nrow(pop))

cat("All checks passed.\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: prior-year
#| eval: !expr nzchar(params$prior_file)
# Side by side with last year's upload, flagging changes over 10 percent.
prior <- read_csv(params$prior_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
upload |>
  inner_join(prior, by = c("part", "line", "cell"), suffix = c("", "_prior")) |>
  mutate(change = (value - value_prior) / value_prior,
         flag = if_else(abs(change) > 0.10 & value_prior >= 10, "review", "")) |>
  gt() |> fmt_percent(change, decimals = 1)
```

# Upload file

```{r}
#| label: upload
#| echo: true
out <- sprintf("EF_%d_upload.csv", params$report_year)
write_csv(upload, out)
cat(nrow(upload), "cells written to", out, "\n")
```

For the portal's key-value format, replace this chunk with the
`IPEDSuploadables` call for Fall Enrollment, or with `writeLines()` per the
import specification. Either way the file is a product of the render.
